newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese pound continues to strengthen-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese pound continues to strengthen-dealers.

text.p: Lebanese banks sold dollars on the Beirut foreign exchange market throughout the week until Friday when the U.S. currency came in demand for commercial transactions, dealers said.
There was no change in the Lebanese pound's steadily strengthening trend against the dollar, they said.

The pound traded at the bottom of the central bank's bid-offer intervention band for the first four days of the week but traded slightly above that level on Friday, a dealer who asked not to be identified told Reuters.
The central bank lowered the band during the week to 1,536-1,545.50 pounds per dollar from 1,536,50-1,546.
"During the whole week except today banks were selling dollars and the central bank bought some dollars, of course," a dealer said.
"Today there was some demand for dollars from commercial banks because of commercial needs. The amounts offered in the market were small," he added.
The dollar traded at 1,536 to 1,536.5 on the first four days of the week but on Friday it traded at 1,537-1,537.5 due to the commercial demand, the dealer said.
